# OA v0.7.20

**Status:** Public development preview

**Release date:** 2026-08-26

**Source:** [`v0.7.20`](https://github.com/realminc/oa/releases/tag/v0.7.20)

## Summary

OA v0.7.20 is the immutable hosted-release repair for the v0.7.19 foundation
source snapshot. It publishes the private `v0.7.1` foundation checkpoint with
corrected sanitizer target ownership. Product code, APIs, numerical behavior,
and performance evidence are unchanged from v0.7.19.

The foundation replaces ordinary hosted-library use across maintained OA code
with bounded OA contracts for containers, ownership, synchronization, time,
filesystem, command-line parsing, Unicode, and platform I/O. It does not claim
linked-binary independence from `libstdc++` or `libc++`.

## Highlights

- OA-owned generated C++ contains zero hosted-library symbols, headers,
  exception tokens, and RTTI tokens under the checked audit.
- Native `oa::Cli<TConfig>`, `oa::CmdCli`, and `oa::OptCli` replace CLI11 and
  fmt; utf8proc 2.11.3 is vendored as an exact private C dependency.
- Sort reaches parity and hash insertion/lookup outperform the host
  implementation on the recorded workload; shared ownership remains slower.
- Hosted ASAN and UBSAN build every executable selected by the `core` CTest
  profile, including `TestCli`.

## Fixed

- Added `TestCli` to the curated ASAN and UBSAN build target list. The v0.7.19
  jobs registered the test through CMake but did not build its executable,
  causing CTest to report one not-run test and correctly block publication.

## Compatibility and migration

- OA remains pre-1.0. Rebuild C++ and Python consumers for this release.
- The C++, Python, model, checkpoint, and execution-plan contracts are
  unchanged from v0.7.19.
- OA-owned code uses `oa::Vec`, `oa::String`, `oa::SharedPtr`, `oa::sort`, and
  `oa::move`; no `oa::std`, `oastd`, or `OaStd*` compatibility layer exists.
- CLI consumers use `oa::Cli<TConfig>`, `oa::CmdCli`, and `oa::OptCli` rather
  than CLI11 types.

## Performance

No performance claim changes in this repair. The accepted fixed-host evidence
is published in the [foundation benchmark](../benchmarks/oaStd.md). Ratios,
absolute medians, spread, provenance, and non-claims remain owned there.

## Verification

| Gate | Result | Evidence scope |
|---|---|---|
| Foundation | Pass | 209 focused correctness tests on the private source checkpoint |
| Release | Pass | 153/153 CTest targets; zero failures and zero skips |
| ASAN `TestCli` | Pass | corrected curated target builds and executes under AddressSanitizer |
| UBSAN `TestCli` | Pass | corrected curated target builds and executes under UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer |
| Python | Pass | host 36, crypto-host 8, GPU 94, crypto-GPU 10; skips forbidden |
| Generation/docs | Pass | generated-source, documentation, architecture, asset, and dependency-ratchet checks |
| Physical GPU | No new route claim | unchanged Intel Iris Xe-qualified foundation paths |

The tagged GitHub workflow owns final hosted CPU-Vulkan, complete sanitizer,
package, wheel, PyPI, release-asset, and checksum evidence. A pending or failed
hosted job is not converted into a pass by this source note.

## Known limitations

- The public-header closure retains the admitted `std::initializer_list`
  language bridge and yaml-cpp adapter.
- VMA and selected private dependencies remain in the complete hosted-library
  and link audit. Binary independence is not shipped.
- Shared ownership remains slower than the host implementation in the measured
  make/copy/release workloads.
- Linux x86-64 is the runtime-qualified foundation platform. Android, Windows,
  Apple, additional compilers, race/fuzz/fault injection, and linked-binary
  independence remain unverified.
- Vulkan Video and GPU routes remain capability, device, driver, and
  queue-topology dependent and fail closed when unavailable.

## Upgrade

Rebuild native consumers and Python wheels, replace CLI11-facing code with the
native OA CLI surface, construct OA path/text values explicitly at external
boundaries, regenerate checked source inventories, and discard stale build,
package, execution-plan, and pre-1.0 binary caches.
